summary: Reuters' round-up of weekend European football centres on Eintracht Frankfurt's 5-1 thrashing of Bayern Munich, which ended the champions' unbeaten Bundesliga run. It also covers RB Leipzig's 3-2 win over 10-man Dortmund, Real Madrid's 1-1 draw at Real Betis, Inter's 4-0 win over Udinese, Atalanta's 3-2 win over Milan and PSG's 2-1 win over Nantes.
one_line: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Bayern Munich 5-1 to end their unbeaten Bundesliga run, in a round-up of weekend results across Europe's top leagues.
key_facts: Eintracht Frankfurt beat Bayern Munich 5-1, snapping the champions' unbeaten Bundesliga run this season, and scored three times in 24 minutes in the first half.

Omar Marmoush scored in the 12th minute, Éric Dina Ebimbe in the 31st and Hugo Larsson in the 36th, the latter after a Joshua Kimmich error; Kimmich pulled one back with a 20-yard shot before the break.
Ebimbe got his second past Manuel Neuer five minutes after the restart and Ansgar Knauff made it 5-1 on the hour.
Frankfurt became the first team in 48 years to score five goals in one hour against Bayern in the Bundesliga, since their own 6-0 win in 1975.

Bayern remain second on 32 points with a game in hand, since the Union Berlin match was postponed due to snow; leaders Bayer Leverkusen have 35 and visit third-placed VfB Stuttgart (30 points) on Sunday.
RB Leipzig beat 10-man Borussia Dortmund 3-2 after Mats Hummels was sent off in the 15th minute, and now sit fourth on 29 points, four ahead of fifth-placed Dortmund.
Real Betis drew 1-1 with Real Madrid after Aitor Ruibal's 66th-minute long-range equaliser cancelled out Jude Bellingham's goal, his 15th in 17 games across all competitions this season.
Real Madrid remain top of La Liga with 39 points, one ahead of Girona, who visit third-placed Barcelona on Sunday.
Inter beat Udinese 4-0 to regain the Serie A top spot, two points clear of Juventus, with goals from Hakan Calhanoglu (penalty), Federico Dimarco, Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martínez (85th minute).
Atalanta beat Milan 3-2 thanks to Luis Muriel's 95th-minute back-heel, after a double from Ademola Lookman; Milan's Davide Calabria had been sent off two minutes earlier.
Paris Saint-Germain beat Nantes 2-1 for their eighth consecutive Ligue 1 win and lead on 36 points, six clear of Monaco, who beat Rennes 2-1.
Randal Kolo Muani scored PSG's winner seven minutes from time after Bradley Barcola's 41st-minute opener and Mostafa Mohamed's 55th-minute equaliser for Nantes.
